units.title: From Web to IoT: Scope, Architecture and Hardware Choice
topics: Choosing the sensors and the board
Requirements as user stories and measurable checks
Eight reasons sensor projects fail, and the cure

sections.title: Choosing the sensors and the board
Requirements as user stories and measurable checks
Eight reasons sensor projects fail, and the cure

summary: A sensor project adds noisy real-world data, batteries, weak networks and costly failures to the concerns of Project II.
KhetSense is the running example; its objectives are measurable, including an accuracy target (O2) and a budget (O5).
The four-layer architecture separates sensing, edge processing, cloud storage and the phone app.
Hardware is chosen from requirements and checked against the budget; the plan is revised with numbers.
The eight failure causes (calibration, battery, gaps, noise, weather, offline, clocks, desk-only testing) guide Units 2 to 5.

units.title: Sensors, Calibration, Noise and Messaging
topics: From soil to count: the ADC
How long does the battery last?
Eight rules for reliable sensor data

sections.title: From soil to count: the ADC
How long does the battery last?
Eight rules for reliable sensor data

summary: The ADC turns a voltage into a count; calibration turns the count into a useful unit and gives a measurable error.
The simulated calibration reached 0.32 points of mean error on new samples; the uncalibrated vendor index was 36 points off.
A moving median removed spikes best (0.58 against 1.67 for raw data).
QoS 1 with ids delivered 96 of 96 readings on a link that lost 30 percent of packets; QoS 0 delivered 64.
Batching the radio lengthened battery life from 87.8 to 165.1 days in the calculation.

units.title: Storing and Analysing Sensor Data: Cleaning, Anomalies and a Forecast
topics: The pipeline from message to advice
Eight uses of data analysis in KhetSense

sections.title: The pipeline from message to advice
Eight uses of data analysis in KhetSense

summary: The pipeline validates, stores once, cleans, analyses and then advises; each step is testable.
Constraints in the database refused 78 duplicates and the impossible value; 8 to 9 percent of readings were missing and recorded as such.
The cleaning rules flagged exactly the three true spikes and left the long gap missing.
Stuck, silent and jumping nodes are detected by three simple rules, with rain used to explain jumps.
The exponential forecast beat persistence (0.58 against 1.31 points) on a small simulated test, and the rule engine turns it into four plain messages.

units.title: The Mobile Client: Offline-first Sync, Screens and Testing
topics: Permissions, privacy and security on the phone
Eight features of a good field-ready mobile client

sections.title: Permissions, privacy and security on the phone
Eight features of a good field-ready mobile client

summary: Native Android with Room and a background worker suits field users best; Flutter or a PWA are alternatives.
Three screens (home advice, plot detail, alerts) answer three questions, and wireframes come before code.
Offline-first design needs a queue, retry and idempotence; the simulation stored 6 unique actions and ignored 5 duplicates.
Stale data must be labelled, and advice must be withheld when data are older than 2 hours.
Test the logic in code and the screens on a device matrix; turn each fixed bug into a permanent test.

sections.title: The demo: ten minutes, with a plan B
Twelve viva questions with short model answers
Eight habits of teams that finish Project III well

summary: A field test turns claims into evidence: the simulated 48-hour log passed four of five objectives and honestly failed O1.
The failed objective is diagnosed (far node, weak link) and a fix is proposed; hiding it would be dishonest.
The report map highlights the sensor-specific chapters; the page budget came to 80 pages with 62 percent technical content.
The demo is rehearsed with a plan B for every live step, including an offline run.
Honesty, consent, licensing and the law apply to sensor data and photographs as much as to code.
